correctness.rationale: The centered edge-cut indicators h_e form the basis dual to oriented edge differences d_e, so W_T=Σ|d_e(u)| on the zero-sum Euclidean sphere. On any sign chamber with ≥2 nonzero edge differences, the restricted W is a positive linear functional on a positive-dimensional sphere: any stationary point at positive height is a maximum, excluding additional minima. Each one-cut unit direction ±u_e is strictly locally minimizing since distinct tree split centered covariances obey |K_ef|<K_ee, implying positive tangent slope. Projecting all other h_f to the tangent gives sharp gamma_e=min_f(1−|K_ef|/K_ee)/sqrt(K_ff−K_ef²/K_ee), attained by a single projected signed cut. On 0<θ<atan(w_e/√2), the distinguished edge difference remains positive and width exactly equals w_e cos θ+gamma_e sin θ at the optimized tangent. Direct Gram algebra gives path gamma=1/sqrt(M(M−1)), star gamma=sqrt((n−2)/(n−1)) and leaf slope ratio n−2. Independent exact rational Gram calculations for paths and stars n=3..10 confirmed the formulas, while the source script checks 1440 small labeled trees. Finite checks do not certify all tree sizes.
